title: A weighting framework to improve the use of emissions scenario ensembles of opportunity
abstract: Abstract Integrated assessment models produce large ensembles of socioeconomic scenarios that are used profusely in climate change research. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), non-governmental organizations or national climate committees often rely on ensemble statistics to identify mitigation strategies and set climate targets. A limitation of such evidence is the opportunistic nature of scenario ensembles: they are an unstructured, serendipitous collection of evidence. Drawing on concepts from physical climate science and ensemble analysis, we present an approach for the flexible, multidimensional weighting of emission scenario data that accounts for relevance, quality and diversity. Our illustrative application to the latest IPCC scenario database demonstrates a reduction in dominance of highly represented models and studies, and sees net-zero emission milestones differ to those originally reported. Our framework formalizes decisions otherwise made in an ad hoc manner, providing a tool contributing to the broader challenge of assessing ensembles of opportunity.
problem: The use of "ensembles of opportunity" for climate research is limited by their unstructured, serendipitous nature, which propagates biases from overrepresented models and lacks a formal way to account for scenario relevance, quality, and diversity, leading to potentially spurious or biased results.
method: This paper proposes a flexible, multidimensional framework that weights individual emissions scenarios in opportunistic ensembles based on their relevance, quality, and diversity to formalize assessment decisions and reduce biases in subsequent analyses.
task: The task is to present a multidimensional weighting framework that accounts for relevance, quality, and diversity to improve the analysis of unstructured and potentially biased emissions scenario ensembles of opportunity.
innovation: This paper presents a flexible weighting framework to improve the use of emissions scenario ensembles by systematically accounting for relevance, quality, and diversity, thus reducing biases from dominant models and formalizing previously ad-hoc assessment decisions.
